Good day miss Niña Anjerrie Baraquil,

Updates for Refund Functionality:

For the refund process, I found a bug:
  • Root Cause: Medusa passes `payment.data` to `refundPayment`, but the `charge_id` was only stored in `payment_session.data`.
  • Impact: Refunds were marked as complete in Medusa but **never actually processed in Clover** - customers were not getting their money back.
  • Fix Implemented: The `refundPayment` method now queries the `payment_session` table to retrieve the `charge_id` when it's not found in `payment.data`.
  • Status: ✅ FIXED - Tested and working

Client's Questions and Answers:

      1. Verify all processes work as expected (as an admin, is it doing what we think it's doing?) (what happens via email at all stages, in medusa and with clover)

    • Refunds initiated from the Medusa admin dashboard are successfully processed through Clover.

    • Full and partial refunds both work correctly.

    • Customers receive a refund confirmation email.

    • Order detail page correctly shows Refunded or Partially Refunded status.

                  ✅ Fixed issues found with the refund flow.

      2. Share with us when and how they work (does it use an API Call to clover? How long does it take on our end? On Clover's end?)

    • Refunds are sent to Clover immediately after an admin triggers them.

    • Clover processes the refund instantly on their side.

    • Funds appear in the customer’s bank account within 3–10 business days, depending on the customer’s bank/card issuer.

    • Note: This delay is standard for all card refunds and is outside our control.


      3. Verify the admin dashboard status is correct (Status is updated)
    • The Orders List page shows “N/A” for refund status.
    • This is expected behavior in Medusa, not a bug.
    • Medusa tracks refund amounts but does not automatically show refund labels (like “Refunded”) in the orders list.
    • The correct refund status is visible on the order detail page.

      4. FEATURE MODIFICATION REQUEST (as admins we want the order status in the dashboard to say "Full Refund Issued". It currently says "N/A")

    • Medusa’s admin dashboard does not natively support custom refund status labels in the orders list view.

    • While it is technically possible to implement this through deeper customization of the admin interface, it would require extending or replacing core admin behavior.

    • This change would be visual only and would not improve or change the actual refund functionality.

    • The correct refund status is already shown on the order detail page, where admins review refund information.


                  Recommendation:
                       Given that refund data is already accurate and visible in order details, leaving the orders list as-is will be fine unless a strong business need arises for list-level labeling. Which we can handle on the custom export sales side(when fixed).



      5. If there is an option for a partial refund, we need functionality to cover that as well. 

    • Partial refunds are fully supported and processed correctly.

    • Medusa accurately tracks refunded amounts and displays partial refund status on the order detail page.

    • Similar to full refunds, adding a “Partial Refund” label to the orders list view would require custom admin changes.

    • This would be a presentation enhancement only and would not affect refund accuracy or behavior.


                  Recommendation:
                       Current behavior provides sufficient visibility into refund status when viewing an order. Additional list-level labeling can be considered in the future if visual reporting becomes a priority.



      6. Additional important question: does the "notes" section for a refund in our dashboard get passed to Clover?

    • Refund notes entered in Medusa are not sent to Clover, due to Clover API limitations.

    • However, these notes are included in the customer’s refund confirmation email, ensuring the customer receives the relevant context for the refund.

    • Internally, refund notes are also stored in Medusa for record-keeping and support reference.


                  Recommendation:
                       Continue using Medusa refund notes for internal tracking and customer communication, without attempting to pass them to Clover.

Thank you.

Good day miss Niña Anjerrie Baraquil ,

Updates:
1. Event Sales Submission (ambassador dashboard)

- The submission window is no longer hidden behind the top navigation bar.
- The window title and the Submit button now stay fixed in place while only the product list scrolls, so a report with 20 or more line items is still easy to finish.
- Products in the picker are now grouped by category. Groups can be collapsed and expanded, each shows a count, and searching automatically opens the groups that contain a match.
- A product with only one option now appears as a single row using the product name. The "Default" variant text is gone.
- SKU codes are no longer displayed on any row. They are still searchable, so typing a SKU still finds the product.
- Every row now shows the product's regular list price on the right.
- Adding a product pre fills the Unit Price with that same regular price, and the ambassador can still type over it with the price they actually sold at.
- Fixed a pricing issue found while doing this: the pre filled price could pick up a member discounted price(Ambassador's 30% discounted rate) instead of the regular price, which would have understated an event report.

2. How Admin approval of an Event works (answering the questions)

- Confirmed, approval does not touch inventory. No stock is deducted.
- Confirmed, no tax is calculated or added.
- Confirmed, the amounts used are exactly the prices the ambassador typed on the Event Report. Nothing is re-read from the catalog, so a 10 to 20 percent event discount is preserved as entered and stays verifiable against the Clover activity for that day.
- Approval only flips the report status to approved and releases the commission. No order, no payment, and no customer record is created.
- Q: Will this adjust the Sales Report by adding a ticket? No. It does not add a ticket today. The Sales Report reads store orders only, and event sales are kept in their own records, so approving an event leaves the Sales Report untouched.
- Recommended approach when we do build it: keep event sales stored separately and combine them only at the report level, with an "include event sales" toggle that is off by default and a breakdown line reading Store Orders plus Event Sales equals Total. That keeps the current Sales Report numbers stable and auditable rather than inventing fake tickets(previous integration. The draft order creation flow).

3. Bulk Group Pricing automation (replaces the manual per-product work)

- New "Bulk Group Pricing" page in the admin dashboard sidebar. Group discounts no longer have to be added product by product.
- Choose an existing price list or create a new one, choose the customer group it applies to, and type the discount percentage.
- Preview runs first and writes nothing. It shows how many products will be priced, how many are skipped and why, and a searchable table of each product's current price next to the new discounted price.
- Applying is a separate confirm step. Changing any field clears the preview, so figures can never be applied without being reviewed first.
- Gift cards are excluded by default with an option to include them.
- After applying, the page reports exactly how many prices were written.

Note: Done applying 30% discount for Ambassador Group Pricing.

4. Product pricing display, related to the above

- Product and shop pages now read the discount from the customer's actual price instead of a hard coded affiliate rule, so ambassadors at 30 percent, affiliates at 20 percent, and any new group added later all display correctly with no further work.
- Fixed a double discount: on the Subscribe and Save option, the plan discount was being applied on top of an already discounted group price. A 117 dollar product was dropping to 84.24 for an affiliate instead of holding at 93.60. Group priced customers now keep their group price as their subscription price, and free shipping remains the subscription benefit for them.
- The notice on the subscribe option now states the customer's real rate, for example "30% off across all products + Free shipping", instead of always saying 20 percent.(Previously hard coded. Now its dynamic based off the Group and group pricing discount percentage)
- Product page category listing cards now show the logged in customer's group price. They previously showed the catalog price to everyone.

Status: all of the above is deployed and live.

(Note: item 1 needs a logged-in ambassador account. Item 3 is safe to explore using Preview, which writes nothing until Apply is confirmed. Item 4 is only visible when logged in as an affiliate or ambassador, since a logged out visitor sees catalog prices by design.)

Thank you.

Checkout Address Issues - Bug Fix Summary

Preview Link: https://deploy-preview-40--stackshift-alwayslove-zmuz.netlify.app/

What customers were experiencing:                                                                                                                                                                                                  

1. Address form kept resetting - After filling in the shipping address and clicking "Continue", the form would jump back to the top and clear the entered information. Customers had to re-enter their address repeatedly, creating a frustrating loop that prevented them from completing checkout.

2. Saved addresses not fully loading - Returning customers who had saved addresses on their account would see most fields pre-filled (city, state, postal code) but the street address field was always blank. This was confusing since the whole point of saving an address is to avoid re-typing it.

3. Switching between address suggestions left old data behind - When customers used the Google address suggestions and picked different addresses one after another, some fields (like city) would get stuck showing information from a previously selected address instead of updating to the new one.

4. Password manager autofill conflicts - Customers using browser extensions like LastPass to autofill their address would run into issues where the form didn't recognize the filled-in data. They had to erase and re-type the address before the form would accept it.

  What was fixed:

1. The address form no longer resets - Customers can now fill in their address and click "Continue" without the form clearing or jumping back to the top. The checkout moves forward to the delivery/shipping step as expected.

2. Saved addresses now fully pre-fill - When returning customers go to checkout, their saved street address now appears along with all other address fields. They can proceed without re-typing anything, or change the address if they want to ship somewhere new.

3. Switching address suggestions properly updates all fields - When customers pick a different address from the Google suggestions, all fields (street, city, state, postal code) now update correctly every time. No more leftover data from previous selections.

4. Password manager and browser autofill now work smoothly - The address field now properly recognizes when information has been filled in by a browser extension or autofill, so customers can proceed without having to re-enter their address.

These fixes apply to both shipping and billing address forms.

Thank you.

Issue:
When a user's session expires while they're still on the Account page, the Promotional Codes and Referral Program sections display a "Please log in" message with a "Retry" button. Clicking the Retry button does nothing useful, it just keeps showing the same error without taking the user to the login page. This creates a confusing experience where the user keeps clicking Retry expecting something to happen.

Fix:
The Retry button has been replaced with a "Go to Login" button when the session has expired. Clicking it now takes the user to the login page so they can sign back in and continue where they left off. For any other type of error (such as a temporary network issue), the button still works as a normal "Retry" to refresh the data.

To Test:
Clear the session cookie 
  1. Open browser DevTools (F12)
  2. Go to Application tab (Chrome) or Storage tab (Firefox)
  3. Under Cookies, find your site's cookies
  4. Delete the connect.sid cookie (Medusa session)
  5. Then navigate to the promotional codes or referral program page
  6. Click the button on the error message.

Thank you.

Hi Miss Niña Anjerrie Baraquil, good afternoon.

I have completed fixing the issues mentioned. 

What happened: Three separate issues were found, all stemming from the same root cause — the website was holding onto login information for up to 24 hours in its memory, even after the actual server session had expired. Think of it like a bouncer checking a printed guest list from yesterday instead of calling the door to verify. The server knew the session was gone, but the browser never got the memo.

This caused three visible problems:

1. Members could still browse after their session expired. Because the site was reading from its own memory rather than checking with the server, members appeared logged in and could freely browse products and collections on a dead session. They only hit a wall when they tried to take an action that required a live connection — like checking out.
2. Clicking a product caused the page to freeze or flicker. When a member on an expired session clicked a product, two redirects to the login page fired at the same time and collided — each one interrupting the other. This is the behavior captured in the investor's video. It was not a crash, but a traffic jam of competing redirects that left the page appearing frozen before eventually resolving.
3. Members got silently stuck at checkout. The checkout page had no session check of its own. Members on expired sessions could land on it normally — their details even appeared pre-filled from cached data — but every action behind the scenes (cart, payment, order) was quietly rejected with no error message and no redirect. Members had no way of knowing their session was gone, so they assumed the site was broken.

What was fixed: The site now verifies the session directly with the server on every protected page load, rather than trusting its own memory. Redirects are controlled so only one fires at a time, eliminating the freeze. The checkout page now checks the session immediately on load. And the login page no longer sends expired-session members back into a loop.

Session timeout: Login sessions are set to expire after 10 hours. Any member idle beyond that will be prompted to log in again on their next click.

Should you have any clarifications, please let me know. Thank you.

After a thorough investigation into the subscription renewal issue reported by Nate (Michael Tanner's Everyday Focus+ subscription missing June and July renewals), I'm sharing my findings, current status, and proposed next steps below for your review before I proceed with any fixes.

Root cause:
In mid-May, we shipped the Subscription Flow + Clover Payment improvements (PCI-DSS compliance work), which changed how customer cards get vaulted for recurring charges. Customers who placed any order after that update ended up with a properly vaulted, reusable Clover token (clover_multipay_token). Customers who hadn't placed any order since before that update were left on the old single-use token type (clover_card_token), which can't be charged a second time. Michael's subscription fell into that gap, which is why June and July's automatic renewals silently failed with no order ever created.

Why July 23 succeeded:
Michael's payment method was actually already upgraded to a valid token by May 15 (via an unrelated one-time purchase), so his card wasn't the blocker by the time of his June/July renewal attempts. Something else in the renewal pipeline was quietly failing before an order could be created. The timing of when it started working again lines up with a checkout/shipping reliability fix that shipped the same day, July 23 — most likely trigger, though not 100% mechanically confirmed yet.

Renewal failures currently have zero logging and zero alerting — unlike checkout, which already logs to payment_error_logs. A renewal that fails before reaching order creation leaves no trace anywhere (no log entry, no incremented failure counter, no customer email), so this could only ever be discovered by a customer noticing a missing shipment.

Member Activity Tracking and Engagement Dashboard (live):

1. What gets recorded

- Every member action on the website is now logged as it happens: account created, successful login, failed login, logout, password reset requested, password reset completed, product viewed, catalog or shop page viewed, item added to cart, checkout started, order completed, and member invite converted.
- Page views and browsing sessions are recorded as well, so you can see the path a member took through the site.
- Time on site is measured two ways: active time counts only while the member is actually looking at the page and interacting, and open time counts from the first action to the last. A member with 18 minutes active against 2 hours open left the tab open and walked away.
- Anonymous visitors who are not signed in are tracked separately, and if they later log in their earlier browsing in that visit is credited to their account.
- Staff pages and unused pages are excluded, so admin desk time never counts as member browsing.

2. Where to find it

- A new Member Activity item now appears in the left menu of the store admin.
- The page opens on a period selector for 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, or all time. This governs every engagement figure on the page. Order history is always all time regardless of the period.
- Five counters sit at the top: total members, anonymous sessions, high engagement with no order, never ordered, and dormant 60 or more days. Each counter is clickable and filters the table below it.

3. Members tab

- One row per member showing name and email, role, last login, number of logins, number of sessions, average active time, engagement as active over open time, last order, total orders, invites converted, and flags.
- The page opens already sorted to show the members worth acting on first, rather than a plain reverse chronological list.
- Every column heading is clickable to sort, and clicking a second time reverses the order.
- Members with no orders show a visible Never marker rather than a blank cell.
- Filters sit directly above the table and are labelled: Search by name or email, Role, and Flag. A Clear filters button appears once a filter is active.
- Roles shown are pulled from the customer groups already set up in the store, so any group created later appears here automatically with no further work.
- Five flags are applied automatically: high engagement with no order, never ordered, browse only, dormant, and active buyer. Wording is neutral on purpose since the same pattern can come from a member researching a first purchase.

4. Activity feed tab

- A running chronological list of everything happening on the site, newest first.
- Filters are labelled and split over two rows. On top: search by name or email, and a filter for whether you are viewing signed in members, anonymous visitors, or everyone. Below: event type, from date, and to date.
- The feed opens on signed in members only. Anonymous browsing is available by changing the filter, since it is usually the larger stream and would otherwise bury member activity.
- Clicking any row belonging to a signed in member opens that member's full history.
- The feed covers the last 180 days and says so on screen.

5. Individual member view

- Opening a member shows their totals: logins, sessions, total and average active time, total open time, orders, lifetime spend, invites sent and converted, last login, and last order.
- A sessions table lists each visit with start and end time, active time, open time, page views, the page they entered on, the page they left from, and device.
- Their own chronological activity feed sits below, filterable by date and event type.

6. Housekeeping and privacy

- Sessions close automatically after 30 minutes of inactivity, so open time does not keep counting after someone closes the browser.
- Detailed event history is kept for 180 days and then removed automatically. The counters and totals are stored separately and are kept permanently, so the all time figures stay correct after old detail is cleared.
- Visitor IP addresses are never stored. Only a scrambled value is kept, which cannot be turned back into an address.

7. Status

Checkout PAY NOW button greyed out (resolved, live in production):

- The greyed out PAY NOW button reported by Eli's member Maria, and seen on your own test orders, has been identified and fixed.
- The cause was a missing billing address on the checkout's internal copy of the order, which the payment button requires before it will activate.
- The order records themselves were never damaged. The billing address was always saved correctly on the store's servers, and no customer data was lost.

Why the page looked completely normal:

- The checkout page displays the shipping address, the items and the shipping cost from information that was arriving correctly, so everything on screen looked filled in and ready.
- The billing address is not displayed anywhere on that step when it matches the shipping address, so its absence was invisible to the customer and to us during testing.
- The payment button checks a wider set of details than the page displays, so it saw the gap that the screen could not show.

Why it happened:

- Each time the cart was refreshed after an update, the commerce platform returned an updated copy of the order.
- By default that platform automatically includes the shipping address, shipping cost, discounts and totals in the refreshed copy, but it does not include the billing address unless it is specifically asked for.
- The refresh was not asking for it, so the returned copy came back without a billing address and replaced the complete copy the checkout had been holding.

Why it came and went:

- Some actions in the checkout return a complete copy of the order and restored the missing detail, so the button would work for one customer and then fail for the next.
- That is why re-entering the card appeared to fix it for order 499 but did nothing for Maria on repeated attempts.
- Waiting or refreshing did not reliably help. This particular check had no automatic retry, unlike the shipping checks, so once the detail was dropped the button stayed inactive until a complete refresh happened to land.

What was changed:

- The cart refresh now explicitly requests the billing address and customer record, so the complete order comes back every time.
- A safeguard was added on the storefront so that if any future response leaves the billing address out, the checkout keeps the copy it already has instead of discarding it.
- Both changes are deployed and live on the production checkout.

Worth noting:

- The button was doing its job. It is designed to refuse payment when the order looks incomplete, which is why no incorrect or unfulfillable orders were charged during this period.
- Affected customers, including Maria, can now complete their orders normally with no action needed on their side.

Thank you.

Hi Nikki Gabato ,

Additional improvements: Unified cross-module content workflow

This supports creating content between agents in a single session. A tool has been added that queries all 4 version tables for the current session; add it to all agents with instruction updates to use it for cross-module requests.

1. Newsletter → Blog
Create newsletter campaign → say "turn that into a blog post"
Expected: Content Gen calls get_session_content("newsletter"), gets content, creates blog

2. Blog → Email
Create blog post → say "email this to someone"
Expected: Email Agent calls get_session_content("blog"), gets content, creates email draft

3. Blog → Social Media
Create blog post → say "make a LinkedIn post from the blog"
Expected: Social Media calls get_session_content("blog"), adapts for platform

4. No regression — fresh session KB workflow
New session, ask "write a blog about AI"
Expected: Existing KB workflow unchanged — searches KB, uses results or stops if nothing found

5. Content type filtering
Create both blog + newsletter → say "turn the newsletter into a social post"
Expected: Only newsletter content returned (not blog)

The normal KB search and agent handoffs work correctly for new-topic requests. Here's why:
The logic is sequential with clear branching. Each agent follows the same pattern:
1. Check for directly provided content — user pastes content inline
2. Check for cross-module content — only triggered when the user explicitly references prior session content (e.g., "turn the newsletter into...", "email the blog content")
3. Otherwise, search the knowledge base — this is the default path for any new topic

The cross-module check is conditional on user intent, not automatic. If a user says:
      "Write a blog post about climate change"

...after having just created a newsletter about pet care, the Content Generation Agent will:
Skip step 2B (no reference to prior content)

Proceed to step 3 → call get_relevant_knowledge_enhanced("climate change")

Use KB results or STOP if nothing found. If KB returns "No relevant knowledge found" AND no cross-module content was retrieved → STOP

For a new-topic request, get_session_content is never called (no cross-module reference), so the STOP condition falls back to the original behavior: no KB results = stop and inform user.

Handoffs are unchanged
The Triage Agent's routing logic is completely independent of the cross-module feature. It still uses multi-signal intent analysis (keywords like "newsletter"/"campaign" vs "blog"/"article" vs "email"/"send to") to route to the correct specialist. The cross-module tool only activates after the correct agent is already handling the request.

Summary: New topic → normal KB workflow. Repurpose request → cross-module retrieval. Handoffs → unaffected.

https://demo.publishforge.cloud/sessions/7fe0ead3-7a6e-4d9a-93ae-9a153c2a50ae

Hello Niña Anjerrie Baraquil ,

Issue: Production SSR/ISR routes (e.g., Careers page) were failing because Netlify Functions were running on Node.js 24, which is incompatible with the callback-style Lambda handlers generated by the project's Next.js 12 runtime.

Solution:

  • Pinned the build NODE_VERSION to 16 in netlify.toml to satisfy next-auth engine requirements.
  • Set AWS_LAMBDA_JS_RUNTIME=nodejs20.x in Netlify to ensure deployed functions use a compatible Lambda runtime instead of Node.js 24.

This restores compatibility without requiring changes to the application's Next.js runtime. Thanks.

The issue was during the customer’s scheduled subscription renewal, the payment attempt failed. Each failed renewal attempt generated a new cart session, and each cart session triggered a separate abandoned-cart email. Because the renewal continued retrying on the same date while the payment failure persisted, this resulted in hundreds of abandoned-cart emails being sent.

Solution:
1. Renewal carts are now properly flagged so they are excluded from abandoned-cart emails
2. Renewal attempts now retry only up to 5 times
3. After 5 failures, the subscription is marked as payment_failed
4. New email notifications inform both the customer and admin when a payment fails
5. Renewal carts are cleaned up automatically to prevent repeated abandoned-cart triggers
6. Renewal is processed on the correct schedule (hourly)
7. Changed kendraszudera@gmail.com cart data to abandoned completed so the old cart sessions created during the bug wont trigger abandoned cart email anymore.


File Changes:
1. Cron Schedule Fix (Critical)
      File: src/jobs/subscription-renewal.ts:74
-Changed from * * * * * (every minute) to 0 * * * * (hourly)


2. Cart Safety - Renewal Cart Exclusion
       File: src/subscribers/abandoned-email-handler.ts:78-83
  - Added check to skip abandoned cart emails for carts with is_renewal or subscription_id in context


3. Cart Context Marking
  File: src/workflows/subscription-renewal.ts:229-233
  - Renewal carts now include is_renewal: true and subscription_id in context

 
4. New Subscription Status
  File: src/models/subscription.ts:23
  - Added PAYMENT_FAILED = "payment_failed" status

 
5. Updated Billing Logic (5 Attempts)
  File: src/services/subscription.ts
  - Added MAX_BILLING_ATTEMPTS = 5 constant
  - Added PAYMENT_FAILED event
  - On failure: increments billing_attempts, updates next_billing_date to next billing cycle
  - After 5 failed attempts: sets status to PAYMENT_FAILED and emits event


 
6. Payment Failed Email Template
  File: src/lib/email-templates/subscription-payment-failed-template.tsx (NEW)
  - Customer version: "Action Required: Payment Failed"
  - Admin version: Shows customer email and subscription details

 
7. Payment Failed Subscriber
  File: src/subscribers/subscription-payment-failed-handler.ts (NEW)
  - Listens for subscription.payment_failed event
  - Sends email to customer and admin when payment fails after 5 attempts

 
8. Cart Cleanup on Job Error
  File: src/jobs/subscription-renewal.ts:64-95
  - On workflow failure, marks renewal carts as completed with renewal_failed: true metadata
  - Only affects carts with is_renewal or subscription_id context (not regular customer carts)

Result:
Renewal-related carts no longer trigger abandoned-cart reminders, failed payments are handled in a controlled manner, and both customers and admins receive clear notifications when a payment cannot be processed.-

1. Existing Member is unable to reset password.
Cause: some customers experienced Medusa reading old/cached environmental variable set before production where the base url of the reset password is set to the development url which is localhost:3000 causing the access page issue.

Solution: hard coded the live url to the email template so customers receive the correct forgot password url on the email.

2. New Member does not receive email after Admin approved account.  Cannot log in.  Cannot reset password to account that despite showing "Approved" for Admin, likely does not exist in the system yet.
Cause: Guest accounts read by Medusa as an existing customer since they were added to the database, but as a guest. Upon approval when system was processing the approval, they read the account as existing, instead of migrating the registration data to the customers data it skipped the step to avoid duplicate accounts.

Solution: Updated approval logic to disregard existing account but has a guest role. Upon approval, if customer exists as guest, their role will be updated to registered customer as well as the registration data migrated to their existing customer data, to retain past orders as guest.

Thank you.

Hi, I've fixed the issue. The issue was on the helper function where it matches the reference type of the link and prepending the "oncology" or "technology" in the link that's why we were able to see the double /oncology/oncology in the link. The query.ts file already handles this cases.

query.ts handles the "/oncology/" prepend
 
"internalLink": coalesce(select(
    linkInternal->_type == "page" || linkInternal->_type == "post" => linkInternal->slug.current,
    linkInternal->_type != null => linkInternal->_type + "/" + linkInternal->slug.current
  ),
    null
  ),


button helper function does the same thing resulting to double /oncology in the link
   
    switch (link?.referenceType) {
      case "oncology":
        hrefPath = `/oncology/${link?.internalLink}`; // <-- problem
        break;
      case "technology":
        hrefPath = `/technology/${link?.internalLink}`; // <-- same here for technology
        break;

      default:
        hrefPath = `/${link?.internalLink}`;
    }

Removing the oncology and technology match fixes the issue.

Hello Ms. April Grace Trocio,

I've looked into this and can confirm that there is no 30-day expiration logic in the website code. The website simply displays all jobs that the Bullhorn API returns as open.

The code queries the Bullhorn API using the following filter:

isOpen: 1 AND isDeleted: 0

This means the website shows every job that Bullhorn considers open and not deleted — there is no date-based filtering on the website side.

You can verify this yourself by visiting the API endpoint used by the website directly in your browser:

https://sesqllulzj.execute-api.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/production/jobs?count=50

This will return all jobs currently being served to the website. At the time of my review, the API returned 47 jobs, with the oldest one dated February 10, 2026 (approximately 44 days ago). There are no jobs older than that, which suggests they are being closed or removed at the Bullhorn level before reaching the website.

Here are a few possible causes worth checking on the Bullhorn side:
  • Bullhorn Admin Settings — There may be an auto-close or auto-expiration policy configured for job orders. This can typically be found under Admin > System Settings or similar areas in the Bullhorn dashboard.
  • Bullhorn Automation (Herefish) — If your organization uses Bullhorn Automation, there may be a workflow rule that automatically closes job orders after a set number of days.
  • Third-Party Integrations — Any third-party tools connected to your Bullhorn account (such as job board integrations, automation plugins, or marketplace add-ons) may have their own rules that auto-expire or close job postings.

I recommend checking these areas or reaching out to Bullhorn support directly to identify which setting or integration is responsible for closing jobs after approximately 30 days.

Thank you!

Hello Roseller Enriquez 

This is better, but still not fully aligned with what we need. We're offering AI services, so we need a bot that reflects that. 

Question: What LLM does this bot use?

Couple of notes: 

1. It suggests pages without links: 



2. If someone wants to contact us, can it submit information to our head of sales? Can it collect that information? Right now, it just says, "go to the contact page."


3. Still too large text blocks. 
Every sentence should be it's own paragraph. Anything more is too much for the chat bot window and feels like a lot. 

4. Does it store questions/responses? 
If so, can we get them sent to us weekly so we can build assets that support the chat interface? For example, if we get a bunch of questions, we can build out a knowledge base for the chat bot and regularly share it with your team to update the bot. 

Or, does it learn from each interaction? 

5. The contact information is wrong:

6. If someone wants to contact the business directly, it should give them the contact information: name and phone number or submit a request to the team. It shouldn't continue to try and support via the chat window. 

7. There's no escalation or fallback:

When it can’t answer (like with “LLM” or “weakpoints”), it gives a generic cop-out. It doesn’t:

  • Apologize

  • Offer to escalate

  • Capture contact info
    It’s stuck in “FAQ mode” and has no sense of when to hand off.

8. No lead capture

Every interaction is a missed conversion. This person was trying to reach a rep. At no point does the bot ask:

  • “What’s your name/email so we can follow up?”

  • “Want me to schedule a call?”

9. Zero strategic framing

The Innovation Analysis answer reads like brochure copy, not consultative discovery. Missed opportunity to:

  • Qualify the buyer

  • Ask industry/context

  • Use any language resembling a real sales convo


10. I tested various prompts to break the bot:

Escalation:
  • “Talk to a human.” 
  • “Can I speak with your head of AI?”
  • “I’m a potential partner, not a client. Who should I talk to?”
  • We’re looking to scope a $200K AI build. Can you connect me with someone today?
  • If I leave my email, will someone get back to me today or next week?”
All of them gave a similar response:



These are the rest of the prompts I used:

AI Credibility Killers

  1. “What model are you running on?” (Do NOT let it say ‘I don’t know’ or fake it)

  2. “What does your AI offering actually include? Be specific.”

  3. “Can you show me a real use case of what Quandary built with AI?”

  4. “Do you use your own AI for internal ops?”

  5. “You’re selling AI but your bot can’t even answer simple questions. Why?”

Knowledge & Utility Gaps

  1. “What’s the difference between your Rapid Innovation service and Innovation Analysis?”

  2. “We use Pipefy. Do you support that?”

  3. “I’m comparing you to TrackVia partners. What’s your edge?”

  4. “What industries do you serve?”

  5. “What’s your average project size and timeline?”

Lead Qualification Logic

  1. “I’m interested in using AI to improve time tracking across 3 offices. Can you help?”

  2. “We’ve got a budget and no internal AI team. What’s next?”

  3. “Can you give me a ballpark price for a 3-month engagement?”

Edge Case / Pushback

  1. “This feels like a generic bot. Are you really using AI?”

  2. “Why should I trust your team with automation?”


Note: The response time from the bot was quite slow.

Solutions: 

1. Replace Generic Logic with Modular Intent-Based Flows

Move away from “if keyword, then page” logic. Instead:

Key intents to build:

  • Service inquiries (e.g., “Do you support Pipefy?” → customized reply per partner)

  • Lead qualification (e.g., “We have a budget…” → ask for name/email and escalate)

  • Pushback responses (e.g., “Why should I trust you with automation?” → trigger a confident proof-based reply)

  • AI credibility questions (“What model do you run?” → answer, and offer internal use examples)

Each intent should have:

  • A short, structured reply

  • Optional follow-up buttons (e.g., “Get connected,” “See an example,” “What’s next?”)

  • An escalation flag when buyer intent is high

2. Add Escalation + Routing Logic

Trigger routing when user inputs include:

  • “We have a budget”

  • “Looking to start a project”

  • “Can I talk to someone?”

  • “We’re comparing vendors”

Flow:

  • Ask for: Name, Email, Company, Goal

  • Pipe that data to: Sales inbox or CRM (even via email, Zapier, Airtable, etc.)

  • Confirm to user:


“Got it. I’ve passed this along to our Solutions Lead. You’ll hear from us shortly. Want to share more context in the meantime?”


3. Implement a Knowledge Base Layer

Hook up the bot to a simple structured knowledge base, even if it’s just a JSON/markdown doc or Notion page at first.

Must include:

  • Key services (with differentiators)

  • Tools supported (Pipefy, Quickbase, Workato, TrackVia)

  • Industry examples

  • Engagement model (timeline, cost ballpark, team involved)

  • Internal use of AI

Avoid relying on auto-indexed web pages. Control the data.


4. Build Logging + Feedback Loop

Track:

  • All user inputs

  • Unanswered questions

  • Escalation rates

  • Repeated drop-offs

Feed those to the internal team weekly to improve:

  • Bot logic

  • Sales readiness

  • Marketing assets

5. UX Clean-up

  • Break every message into single-line paragraphs (readability)

  • Remove long-winded “I’m sorry” intros

  • Include real names and roles for escalation (e.g., “I can connect you with Dan, our AI Solutions Lead”)

  • Requires correct URL setup — broken or missing query parameters may hide important sections.

Hello Ms. April Grace Trocio,

Following up on the text to HTML ratio investigation. I ran manual checks today on several pages that were flagged at 0.00% in the Semrush report. As shown in the attached screenshots, those same pages are now scoring between 9 to 13%, confirming the fixes have taken effect.

The website runs on a framework that automatically includes a large block of data in every page's HTML for it to function properly. This block is called NEXT_DATA and it contains all the page content in a structured format used by the site internally. It inflates the HTML size and naturally lowers the ratio, regardless of how much visible text is on the page. You can see this yourself by visiting any page on the site, right clicking, selecting View Page Source, and searching for NEXT_DATA. You will find a very large block of code that is not visible text but still counts as HTML, which is what pulls the ratio down.

Removing or reducing HTML in the website would require major changes to how the site is built and would need thorough testing to ensure nothing breaks.

Happy to discuss further if needed.

Please let me know if you have any questions. Thank you.

Hello all!

Hello Ms. April Grace Trocio,

I reviewed the Semrush report and found two issues causing the low text-to-HTML ratio scores across the site.


Blog posts and standard pages (ratio 0.00) — Page content was being hidden from search engine crawlers due to a rendering bug in how the pages were built. The content was only loading after JavaScript ran in the browser, which search engine crawlers do not wait for. This meant crawlers were seeing a blank page with no readable text, resulting in a 0.00 ratio. I fixed this so the content is now included directly in the page's HTML, making it fully visible to crawlers as soon as the page loads. These pages should see the biggest improvement.


Knowledge Base articles (ratio 0.03–0.09) — The sidebar navigation showing categories and related articles was also loading via JavaScript after the page, meaning crawlers could not see it either. I moved this to load server-side so it is part of the page HTML from the start. The ratio on these pages may still read lower than ideal since the articles themselves contain less text compared to a full blog post — adding more written content to each article would help push these scores higher.


Please note that search engines and tools like Semrush do not reflect changes immediately — it can take days to a few weeks for the updated scores to appear depending on when they next crawl the site. If the scores remain low after a few weeks, please let me know and I will investigate further.

Thank you!

Step-by-Step Troubleshooting Guide

Please work through these steps in order:

Step 1: Test in a Private/Incognito Window

  • Action: Open the PDF link in an Incognito window (Chrome) or Private window (Firefox/Safari).

  • Why this helps: This temporarily disables browser extensions (like ad-blockers or privacy tools) that can sometimes interfere with file downloads. If the PDF loads here, the issue is likely a browser extension.

Step 2: Test on a Different Network

  • Action: If you're in the office, please try accessing the PDFs from a personal device on a home network or a phone using mobile data (with WiFi turned off).

  • Why this helps: This determines if the problem is related to your office firewall, network proxy, or security settings. If it works on a different network, the issue is network-related.

Step 3: Try a Different Browser or Device

  • Action: If you normally use Chrome, please try accessing the PDFs with Microsoft Edge, Firefox, or Safari.

  • Why this helps: This helps rule out a temporary bug or corruption within a single browser's installation.


Step 4: Provide Specific Error Details (If the issue persists)
If the PDFs still fail to load after the steps above, please provide us with the following details. This information is crucial for our investigation:


  • The exact URL of one or two specific PDFs that are failing.

  • A screenshot of the entire browser window, including the address bar and any error message.

  • The name and version of the browser you are using (e.g., "Chrome Version 128.0.6613.120").

  • The specific error message or code (if any) that appears.

We are continuing to monitor your site from our end for any performance anomalies. Your collaboration in this process is invaluable. Please let me know the results of these tests at your earliest convenience so we can proceed with the correct solution.

The “New Product” toggle has been removed, and the code now uses only the product’s published date to control the functionality of both the “New” flag banner and the “View New Products Only” checkbox.

  • A product will display the “New” flag banner if its published date is within the last 90 days. Once the product is older than 90 days, the banner will automatically disappear.

The main issue why you deleted it is that the "Lupe Wall and Renata Wall from Bruck" were USED at "Feature_I".

Deletion Restriction Due to Data Dependencies
When attempting to delete "Lupe Wall and Renata Wall from Bruck" from the What's Hot section, StackShift blocks the action because that data is actively referenced by Feature_I.
Why the deletion is blocked:
Feature_I dynamically pulls in "Lupe Wall and Renata Wall from Bruck" as part of its content. If the record is deleted directly from What's Hot, Feature_I would be left with a broken or missing reference — essentially orphaned data.
To prevent this, StackShift enforces a dependency check: "This record cannot be deleted because it is currently in use by Feature_I."
How to delete it cleanly:
To fully remove "Lupe Wall and Renata Wall from Bruck" without leaving broken references, you must first remove it from every section that uses it — in this case, Feature_I — before (or simultaneously when) deleting it from What's Hot.

General Rule:

If a piece of data is shared or referenced across multiple sections/features, it must be removed from all dependent locations before it can be deleted from its source. Because the data is dynamic, deleting it at the source without cleaning up its references will cause data loss or broken content in the sections that depend on it.

3. Product Page SEO Enhancements

Added essential SEO meta configurations within the <Head> component of product pages:
Canonical Tags: Prevent duplicate content issues by specifying the preferred URL.
Robots Meta Tag: Controlled indexing behaviour (index, follow) to ensure crawlability.
Meta Description: Dynamically generated descriptions with truncation logic for SERP optimisation.

Implemented using next/head in dynamic route pages.
Canonical URL derived from the current slug to maintain consistency.
Description sanitisation and length handling are applied programmatically.
Ensured no duplication or conflict with existing SEO tags.


4. The shop page us filtering. When a user applies filters, the URL updates to reflect the active facets

The problem was that no matter which filters a visitor selected, the canonical tag was always pointing back to the plain /shop address. So from Google's perspective, every filtered page looked like a duplicate of the main shop page — and Google would refuse to list them separately in search results.
This meant that a page like "Hardware > Polished Chrome > In Stock" — which could be a valuable search result for someone looking for exactly that — was invisible to Google.

What was fixed?
The canonical tag now updates automatically to match whatever filters are active. So if a visitor is browsing the Hardware category, the canonical tag correctly identifies that filtered page as its own unique page — and Google can index and rank it independently.
Filters that are genuinely useful for search (like category and brand) are kept in the canonical. Filters that are not useful for search (like sort order and price range) are stripped out, keeping things clean.



5. Heading Structure -
A well-structured H1 helps search engines like Google clearly understand what a page is about by defining its main topic in a straightforward way. This improves how the content is interpreted and aligned with search queries, especially when the H1 is consistent with the page title, metadata, and overall content. It also creates a logical structure for the page, making it easier for crawlers to parse and for users—including those using assistive technologies—to navigate the content. While a strong H1 contributes to better relevance and overall content quality signals, it does not directly solve indexing issues in Google Search Console. Its real value is in strengthening the page’s clarity and coherence, which supports SEO performance when combined with other factors like unique content and proper technical setup.

Algolia Filtering & Navigation Issue – Summary

Issue

  • Incorrect Initial Render (page overlapping before correct content loads)

  • Navigation Jitter and high Layout Shift (CLS) during interactions

  • Latency between initial render and final content display

Root Cause

  • Caused by Algolia routing integration (createInstantSearchRouterNext)

  • Search state was being synchronized with the URL

  • Triggered implicit Next.js router.push() on every refine

  • Resulted in unintended navigation and stale state being rendered before update

Fix Implemented

  • Removed routing configuration from InstantSearch

  • Disabled URL synchronization for search state

  • Replaced all <a> tags / href usage with controlled refine() calls

  • Implemented fully client-side filtering and pagination logic

Improvements After Fix

  • Eliminated unexpected navigation and fallback to /shop

  • Resolved incorrect initial render and page overlap issue

  • Reduced layout shift, resulting in smoother UI transitions

  • Improved response time by removing redundant routing and re-renders

  • Filters, sorting, and pagination now operate fully client-side

  • More stable and predictable UI state during user interactions

  • Validating the script integration

  1. Cross-brand access — The order form SKU search had no brand restriction. A Hickory Hardware-only account could type any BK SKU and add it to an order. Fixed: the search endpoint now filters results to the customer's assigned brand, and the order creation endpoint now validates every item against the customer's brand before creating the cart. A Hickory-only account will no longer see or submit BK products.

  2. Incorrect pricing — I investigated the $11.27 price on B076640-CBZ (list price $18.99, sale price $11.27). No code change is needed here — this is a Swell data/configuration issue.

Here is what I found: BK variants have price rules defined for customer groups 1–19 and 26–30. Group 20 (the group assigned to this account) has no price rule on BK variants. When Swell cannot find a matching group price rule, it falls back to the sale_price value on the variant — which is $11.27 — even though the sale toggle is currently off.

To resolve this, someone with Swell admin access would need to do one of the following on BK variants:

  • Clear the sale_price field on BK variants where the sale toggle is off, so there is no fallback value for Swell to use, or
  • Add a Group 20 price rule set to MSRP on BK variants, so Swell uses the correct price instead of falling back

That said, since the cross-brand fix (issue 1) is now deployed, Group 20 accounts are blocked from ordering BK products entirely, so this pricing fallback will not occur again for this account going forward.

Please let me know if you have any questions or if something seems off.


Thank you

Hello Ms. April Grace Trocio,

I've investigated the Swell webhook delivery failures reported on April 8, 2026. Here's a summary of what was found and what was done to resolve it.


The webhook endpoint (/api/webhooks/product-revalidate-830ecf0254sh91) was timing out before it could respond to Swell. Swell has a 10-second timeout for webhook delivery, any endpoint that doesn't respond within that window is marked as a delivery failure. The webhook was performing a full page revalidation process inline, which was taking longer than the allowed time, causing Swell to log the repeated delivery failures.


The image below shows the Netlify request logs during the time of the failures. The 499 status codes indicate that Swell closed the connection before receiving a response, while the requests that returned 200 were for products outside the Hickory Hardware and Heritage Designs catalogs, which skipped revalidation and responded immediately.





The second image is from Swell's official webhook documentation, confirming the 10-second timeout behavior and the retry/disable policy that triggered the alert sent to the client.





Upon investigation, I found one contributing factor:
  1. The revalidation process was running steps sequentially that could be handled simultaneously, adding extra time to each request.

What Was Done


  • Refactored the page data fetching to run Sanity CMS and Swell API calls in parallel, reducing the time needed to regenerate a product page.

The fixes have been deployed to production. Swell webhook delivery is now succeeding.


Let me know if you have any questions.


Thank you!

Hello Ms. April Grace Trocio,


To provide some context on how the HLF Cases page works, the year boxes in the sidebar are data-driven, meaning a year box will only appear on the page once there is at least one case added under that year. This is why the 2025 box was not showing, there were no 2025 cases added yet, and there was no 2025 year category created to assign cases to.

To allow cases to be assigned to a year, a Year Category must first exist. I have gone ahead and created the 2025 Year Category for you, so you can now start adding 2025 cases right away.
To add a 2025 case:


  1. In StackShift Studio, navigate to Legal Alert and click New
  2. Fill in the case details (Case Title, Court, Case No., Attorneys, Case Details)
  3. In the Year field, select 2025
  4. Publish the case
  5. Navigate to Pages → HLF Cases page → Features section
  6. In the List of Legal Alerts field, click Add Item, search for the case you just created, and add it
  7. Publish the page
  8. Please allow a few minutes for the changes to reflect on the live site, as the page goes through a build process in the background after publishing

Once a 2025 case is added and published, the 2025 box will automatically appear above 2024 on the HLF Cases page.


For Future Years (e.g., 2026)


When the time comes to add a new year, no code changes are needed. You have two options to create a new Year Category:

  • Option A: Navigate to "Categories by Year", click New, enter the year (e.g., 2026), and publish. Then follow the steps above to create and add cases under that year.
  • Option B: When creating a new "Legal Alert", click the Year field and select Create New directly from there — this will create the year category on the spot without needing to navigate to "Categories by Year" separately.

Once at least one case is published under a year and added to the page, the year box will appear automatically.
